record.name: Tempest Harpyrazor
record.title: The Sky-Splitting Storm Hunter
record.anatomy_plan:
Overall body plan: A giant, powerfully built raptor shaped like an eagle but stretched to Quetzalcoatlus size, built to soar like a pterosaur and strike like a falcon, wrapped in living storm clouds like a thunderbird.

Size & frame (Quetzalcoatlus + Harpy Eagle):
- Height on ground about 4–5 m when standing on all fours, with a long, lightly built torso from Quetzalcoatlus.
- Limbs are thick and muscular like a Harpy Eagle’s legs but long enough to work as front struts for launch, echoing the Quetzalcoatlus quadruped takeoff.
- Hollow but reinforced bones: mostly Quetzalcoatlus-style ultralight skeleton, with extra thickened joints and talon bones inspired by Harpy Eagle.

Wings (Thunderbird + Quetzalcoatlus + Peregrine):
- Wingspan around 13–14 m: slightly less than pure Thunderbird legend, more than Quetzalcoatlus.
- Overall shape: long, narrow, pointed like a giant peregrine’s scythe-wings, mounted on a Quetzalcoatlus-style shoulder and membrane frame.
- Feathers along the leading edge and outer third of the wing (Thunderbird + falcon), trailing into leathery pterosaur membrane closer to the body for glide efficiency.
- Wingtips constantly prickle with static and tiny lightning forks (Thunderbird); fine control feathers give peregrine-style steering at high speed.

Head & senses (Harpy Eagle + Peregrine + Quetzalcoatlus):
- Skull length and spear-like beak length between Quetzalcoatlus and Thunderbird, but cross-section more raptor-like: hooked tip over a stabbing spear ridge.
- Huge, forward-facing eyes with peregrine-level vision and harpy-like depth sense; bony crest curve from Quetzalcoatlus over the back of the skull, fringed with a Harpy Eagle’s double feather crest.
- Nostrils and ear openings shielded under small bony ridges to protect from hurricane winds.

Talons & feet (Harpy Eagle + Thunderbird):
- Rear feet massively overbuilt, scaled up Harpy Eagle talons the size of swords; inner talon exaggerated into a lightning “spike” channel.
- Claws and lower legs wrapped in storm-charged scales that insulate the rest of the body when it dumps lightning through its grip.
- Front limbs end in smaller but still serious grasping claws, mainly for launch and climbing, not main weapons.

Tail & control surfaces (Peregrine + Quetzalcoatlus):
- Long, stiff tail with a diamond-shaped feather fan at the end like an oversized falcon tail, used as a rudder in dives.
- Feathers over thin pterosaur tail bones: light but powerful steering.

Storm organs & electricity (Thunderbird + all flyers):
- A specialized “storm bladder” in the chest stores electrical charge harvested from friction in fast dives and from ambient storms.
- Air sacs from pterosaur/falcon design help pump huge amounts of air through the body, cooling it when charge builds up.
- Conductive feather shafts and wing bones route electricity to wing edges and talons.

Feathers, hide, and insulation (Thunderbird + Harpy Eagle + Peregrine):
- Dense, waterproof body feathers like a Harpy Eagle’s but slate-grey like Thunderbird and Peregrine backs, with lighter barred chest.
- Downy underlayer for high-altitude cold; outer feathers are slightly metallic-looking, helping carry current.
- Wing membranes between feathered “fingers” are smoky-grey, semi-translucent when backlit.

Storm cloak (Thunderbird):
- Skin micro-pores vent warm, moist air from its body, which, when mixed with rapid wingbeats and static, can puff into a tight personal cloud.
- This cloud is thin at low power (a glowing mist sheath) and can thicken into a thunderhead bubble around it in full storm mode.

Overall: one unified species, a gigantic raptor-pterosaur storm rider that uses pterosaur frame and falcon speed, harpy talons, and thunderbird storm organs to rule the skies—but must stay high, cool, and moving, or it overheats and becomes clumsy.

abilities.name: Thunder Dive
abilities.blurb: It folds its giant wings and dives like a falcon, slamming down with a lightning blast on impact!

abilities.name: Stormcloak Veil
abilities.blurb: It whips up a spinning thundercloud around its body, hiding inside flashing mist as it glides.

abilities.name: Razor Gale Talons
abilities.blurb: It rides a rushing gust between trees and cliffs, twisting like a harpy to grab foes with storm-charged claws.

abilities.name: Sky Vault Launch
abilities.blurb: It crouches on all fours, then vaults into the sky in one huge leap, catching air and vanishing on the wind.

strengths: Incredible dive speed and aerial burst attacks from high above, especially in stormy weather.
Can create its own stormy cover, making it hard to see and predict when it will strike.

Talons hit extremely hard and can carry a jolt of lightning to stun or knock out large targets on contact instead of just slashing them.
- Superb vision and maneuverability make it dominant in open sky and along cliffs, hard to ambush from below.
- Excellent long-distance glider; can patrol huge areas of sky with little energy if it stays high and rides winds.
weaknesses: Lightweight hollow bones and wide wings make it vulnerable in tight spaces; it struggles badly inside dense forests, caves, and city streets.
If its storm bladder overheats from too many lightning moves in a row, it must glide away and cool off, losing access to its strongest powers for a while.

Large body and long wings make land movement slow and awkward; on the ground it is much easier to surround and corner it.
- Feathers and membranes can get soaked and heavy in cold rain if it isn’t building its own warm storm, reducing lift and dive speed.
- Its giant size makes stealth on land almost impossible; once perched low or grounded, it is easy to spot and plan around.
record.visual_spec:
A colossal flying hunter with the body shape of an eagle stretched to the size of a small airplane. Standing height around 4–5 meters, with a 13–14 meter wingspan. The torso is powerful but lean, built like a giant bird of prey crossed with a pterosaur, chest deep and muscular, hips narrow, bones long and light.

The head is long and narrow like a spear-beaked pterosaur, but ends in a sharp hooked raptor tip. Along the back of the skull runs a tall Quetzalcoatlus-style bony crest, edged with a Harpy Eagle’s double fan of black and grey feathers that can flare up when it’s excited. Eyes are huge, round, and golden-yellow, set forward like an owl or eagle so it looks very focused and hunting. Nostrils and small ear openings are tucked under subtle bone ridges.

The beak is slate-grey, almost metallic, with a smooth spear ridge along the top and a darker hooked end, giving it both a stabbing and tearing look. The upper beak has tiny lightning-shaped etchings glowing faint blue-white when its powers are charged.

Its neck is thick and flexible, clothed in dense feathers that grade from pale smoky-white on the throat to charcoal grey on the back of the neck. Over the shoulders and back, the feathers are smooth and tight like a peregrine falcon’s, dark slate-blue to charcoal with a faint sheen, as if they hold metal. The chest and belly are lighter, cream to pale grey, with dark horizontal bars like a giant peregrine’s breast pattern.

The wings are massive and dramatic: long, narrow, and sharply pointed like a falcon’s scythe wings, but with a pterosaur’s inner structure. Closest to the body, the wing surface is a smooth, leathery membrane of smoky grey, stretched between long finger-like bones. From the middle outward, this membrane is covered in broad flight feathers, which narrow into razor-sharp, lance-like primaries at the tip. These outer feathers are the darkest, almost storm-cloud black with silver edges. At the very tips, tiny forks of white-blue lightning crackle and jump from feather to feather.

The tail is long and stiff, ending in a diamond-shaped fan of feathers. The tail fan is patterned like a scaled-up falcon tail: dark bars on a grey base, spreading wide when it turns and snaps shut when it dives. When seen from behind in a dive, the tail and wings make a triangular, arrowhead shape.

The legs are extremely muscular and thick, scaled like an eagle’s but far larger. Scales are golden-grey, with a faint metallic shine. Each rear foot bears four enormous talons; the inner talon on each foot is longer than a human forearm, curved like a sickle, with a darker tip that glows very faintly blue when charged. The front limbs, used for launch and climbing, end in smaller but still serious claws, more like strong pterosaur hands with hooked black talons. When walking on all fours, the creature moves a bit like a giraffe-tall pterosaur, chest low and wings partly folded.

The whole body is wrapped in a thin halo of mist and cloud. Around the wing edges and along the spine, vapor swirls constantly, twisting into little streamers as it moves. In calm mode, this looks like a light, ghostly fog hugging the feathers. In battle mode, the fog thickens into a tight thundercloud cloak, with darker, churning cloud wrapping the body, flickers of white and blue lightning shining inside, and occasional thin bolts snapping from wingtip to wingtip. When it flaps hard, you can imagine the air behind it as rolling, layered storm cloud, with rainlike mist sheeting off its wings.

Color palette focuses on slate-blue, charcoal grey, smoky white, and pale cream, with electric blue-white highlights in the lightning and eye glow, and golden tones on claws and eyes. Textures mix soft, layered feathers on the head, neck, chest, and outer wings; taut, leathery membrane on the inner wings; hard, ridged scales on feet and lower legs; and smooth, slightly glossy beak and crest. Overall silhouette is that of a gigantic, streamlined predator bird, merged with a pterosaur’s long limbs and tail, crowned with storm cloud and sparks.
record.fun_fact: When it practices diving without using lightning, it still pulls so much air behind it that it draws a tiny spiral cloud ring through the sky where it just passed.
